sources.title: Sheldon Axler, Measure, Integration and Real Analysis
sources.locator: Section 3A, printed p. 74: the convention immediately before Definition 3.2; read with the surrounding S-partition, lower Lebesgue sum, and nonnegative-integral definitions on printed pp. 74–75.

contents.name: Section 3A, p. 74: the convention interpreting 0·∞ and ∞·0 as 0 in the lower-Lebesgue-sum/integration setup
contents.reason: This supports the adopted zero value as a formula convention in integration. The authored item extends it only through its separately typed function-level operation and local exhaustive-case verification; it does not attribute that total operation or field laws to Axler.

sources.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory
sources.locator: Section 3.2, printed pp. 34–36 (PDF pp. 38–40): Definition 3.3 and Propositions 3.4–3.7; read the complete section, including the stated definedness restriction for extended-real-valued products.

contents.name: Section 3.2, Definition 3.3 and Propositions 3.4–3.5: measurable functions and threshold-set criteria
contents.reason: The authored definition accepts arbitrary functions and makes no measurability assertion, so these criteria are not used.

contents.name: Section 3.2, Proposition 3.6 discussion: extended-real products are measurable only when the pointwise scalar products are defined
contents.reason: This records the partial scalar-product boundary that the new function-level operation keeps distinct. Hunter's measurable-product result is not used as a proof of the new total operation.

contents.name: Section 3.2, Proposition 3.7: lattice and absolute-value measurability
contents.reason: The authored item claims no lattice or measurability property.
